Cloud data for each player is broken into two sections - one section is done in the order of play. Each player builds on the same data so the data across all four players should be identical for this. I.e. Player 1 starts by setting the seed and taking his turn. The other players copy player 1's cloud data into their own as they receive it. When it's the next player's turn it works organically because the other players will naturally be in a waiting state. This ensures they all stay 100% in sync. In addition to this, we have a number at the beginning of the play data that says what position into the play data we're starting. When the game begins, this will be at zero for each player. When a player has acted on data it can remove that data from the beginning of the cloud storage if that data exists for all players. After removing you can increase the starting offset at the beginning by however much has been removed.

We also have dynamic storage - data which can happen out of turn. This includes Uno!, Uno challenge! and messages. We'll deal with those afterwards and update this comment at that point.

Messaging uses first two numbers of each cloud variable - message counter and message index. That's it :)

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

This is largely outdated waffle but probably contains some useful info. I'll update this when I have time to do a full pass-through of this file to neaten up the code!
________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


active counter: 1 digit
name section counter: 1 digit
name section: _letters in name sections * 2 digits (8)
state: 1 digit - in lobby, playing, inviting, accepting, declining

state dependent data:

    state.idle - no digits
    state.inviting - uses maximum of maxPlayersInGame*2 (if we ensure maximum number of game slots is 99)
    state.inviting randomly - one digit for number of players we want in game + uses maximum of maxPlayersInGame*2 (if we ensure maximum number of game slots is 99)
    state.accepting - two digits (game slot we're accepting)
    state.declining - two digits (game slot we're declining)
    state.playing - defined per game

    -> minimum data is maxPlayersInGame*2, maximum data is max(maxPlayersInGame*2, digitsForPlayerGameData)



It's important for each player to only need to write to one single cloud variable. That write will contain an active counter (to show player is online), a state counter (updated when written to so it can be determined if the write was successful) and any other game data required.

I'll go for active counter updates once every two seconds. I'm working on the assumption that writes are queued at server side so always get through.

Issues are that other queued writes at the server could easily overwrite each other. Consider three counters - AABBCC. We start at 00:00:00. What if two updates 01:00:00 and 00:01:00 are queued? The second will overwrite the update of the first. Probably the best thing to do is for each instance to update its section of a cloud variable every n frames where n is a random number between 4 and 30. Each cloud variable will have a maximum of 16 players so this should hopefully be enough. Might have to use a long period of time for initial activity check and before any dropouts are assumed (ten seconds maybe?)

☁ Cloud 1
--------------
32 characters: Name of the player of the last (successfully) updated slot counter
_Max Players x 2 characters: player slot counters

While active, a player will increment its counter every 0.1 seconds. We are able to detect empty slots by comparing a snapshot of this cloud variable with another taken half a second later. We are also able to scan names for all active slots by monitoring this variable.

Per-player cloud data (16 bytes)
2 digits: active counter
1 digits: name section index
8 digits: name section data
1 digits: game play state
3 digits: game play data

This means the full name won't be accessible instantly but we should know which players are active and which aren't within a short time frame.

"debug lobby?" setting
-----------------------------
I implemented this to be able to test a game locally and ensure the logic for cloud multiplayer is in place correctly. I make no guarantee it's going to relay 100% well to online cloud usage but it will at least help iron out any obvious mistakes,

Be careful with the setting for _local test players as the processing required will quickly escalate. I've tested it here with large numbers (100+) so you're probably only likely to need to test with a handful for your own games (and assume it'll work up to "_max players".

Use the "Lobby.Change active player" receiver to update the entire display if you're debugging multiple players locally.

Make sure this is set to "false" when you share the game!

Why is everything cloud-related crammed into a single sprite?
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Why did I put the font and everything else into one single sprite? Because I wanted to make it easy to add to other projects and this means simply backpacking the one sprite to do so.

Can I use the font system for other purposes?
--------------------------------------------------------------
I guess so, if you really want to. As it's included in the lobby sprite it's fairly lobby-specific. It's also clone-based rather than pen-based as I wanted the clarity of graphics and also the extra performance. You're probably better off using a different font-system for generic purposes.

Maintaining privacy
--------------------------
Okay, so this isn't so memory efficient. Maintaining privacy means keeping lists as "this sprite only" and that means that every clone is going to contain its own copy of that list. I may revisit this at some point and use "for all sprite" lists with Debug.SpriteName designations.
